slides.text: A function is a named block of code. You write it once with `fn`, and run it whenever you want by using its name.

Writing a function does not run it. Only a **call** runs it: the name, then `()`, then `;`.

`main` is a function too. Rust calls it for you when the program starts, and from there you call the others.
Function names are written in `snake_case` and say what the function does, like `print_banner` or `show_menu`.

slides.text:
A variable made with `let` inside a function belongs to that function. It exists while the function runs, and no other function can see it.

Two functions may even use the same name for different variables.
A `const` written outside every function is different: all the functions of the file can read it.
The order of definitions does not matter. `main` can call a function written below it, as long as it is in the same file.

chunks.guide: The constant is outside every function, so `show_status` can read it. `health` exists only inside `show_status`.

notes.text: A local variable: only this function sees it.

chunks.guide: `main` reads the same constant, then calls the function.
